name: LLM+P (Large Language Models + Classical Planners)
org: University of Texas at Austin and Sony AI
one_liner: An LLM translates a natural-language planning problem into a formal PDDL problem file, and the Fast Downward classical planner computes a sound or minimum-cost plan.

loop.proposes: A PDDL problem specification (objects, initial state and goal predicates) translated from natural language by GPT-4
loop.judged_by: The Fast Downward classical symbolic planner (classical planners LAMA and FDSS) running against the domain action schema
loop.steers: Fast Downward searches the symbolic state space to return a verified plan, which is translated back into natural language

headline_result: Across seven standard International Planning Competition (IPC) domains including Blocksworld, Barman, Floortile, Grippers, Storage, Termes and Tyreworld (20 tasks per domain), LLM+P with GPT-4 and in-context examples solved the majority of tasks with valid, cost-minimizing plans, whereas direct GPT-4 plan generation failed on almost all tasks in Barman, Floortile, Storage and Termes.
caveat: LLM+P requires a human expert to supply the PDDL domain file (action preconditions and effects) in advance, and its one-shot translator has no validator-repair loop when the LLM emits syntax errors, undeclared objects or inverted goal predicates.
beyond_harness_note: The LLM does not search for action sequences at all; it compiles natural language into PDDL so Fast Downward can perform sound symbolic search.
generative_model: GPT-4 (frozen) with in-context PDDL problem examples

sources.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency

verification.notes: Verified against Bo Liu et al., arXiv:2304.11477 (2023) and the Cranial-XIX/llm-pddl repository. Confirmed the 7 IPC benchmark domains (20 problems each), use of Fast Downward (SEQ-OPT-FDSS-1 / LAMA), requirement of a human-provided domain PDDL file, and failure modes from one-shot PDDL translation errors.
